definitions.explanation: A traditional Japanese form of wrestling where two opponents try to force each other out of a circular ring or make them touch the ground with anything other than their feet.

examples.japanese: {相撲|すもう}を{見|み}に{国技館|こくぎかん}に{行|い}った。
examples.english: I went to Kokugikan to watch sumo.

examples.japanese: {子供|こども}たちが{相撲|すもう}を{取|と}っている。
{大相撲|おおずもう}の{力士|りきし}に{会|あ}った。
examples.english: I met a professional sumo wrestler.

notes:
{相撲|すもう} is the traditional Japanese sport of sumo wrestling.

Common collocations:
- {相撲|すもう}を{取|と}る (to wrestle sumo)
- {大相撲|おおずもう} (professional sumo)
- {相撲|すもう}{部屋|べや} (sumo stable)
- {相撲|すもう}{取|と}り (sumo wrestler - colloquial)

Sumo vocabulary:
- {力士|りきし} (sumo wrestler)
- {横綱|よこづな} (grand champion)
- {大関|おおぜき} (champion rank)
- {土俵|どひょう} (sumo ring)
- {場所|ばしょ} (sumo tournament)
- {国技館|こくぎかん} (Kokugikan - sumo arena in Tokyo)

Cultural note: Sumo is considered Japan's national sport ({国技|こくぎ}) and has deep connections to Shinto traditions.
